channel.title: Infrastructure Club Travel Guide
channel.description: Latest places added to the travel guide

item.title: “Hollywood Reservoir Dam” added in Hollywood, United States
item.description: Walkable dam on a lovely short hike. The last great public work built by William Mulholland, architect of the canals and aqueducts that brought water to modern Los Angeles.

item.title: “Laaksaare Sadam” added in Räpina, Estonia
item.description: In the Winter you can get a hovercraft to Piiri from here. https://transport.tartumaa.ee/en/ferry-transportation/

item.title: “Museum of Industry Ghent” added in Gent, Belgium
item.description: Great museum showcasing history of textiles and typography/graphic design in Gent, with lots of machines over the years - you can even buy things from the shop made from these machines

item.title: “Sint-Annatunnel” added in Antwerpen, Belgium
item.description: Tunnel under the river with WOODEN ESCALATORS! Plus heritage adverts inside and art deco buildings!

item.title: “Wouda pumping station” added in Lemmer, Netherlands
“Petrova Gora Spomenik” added in Vrginmost, Croatia
item.description:
The monument to the uprising of the people of Kordun and Banija.
A vast, but abandoned building. It once was going to hold a congress hall, library, museum, and cafe. It's easy to get into and the structure is sound - solid steps to walk up inside.
To get there from Zagreb, you can go on a tour with Swanky Travel: https://swanky-travel.com/tour/urban-explorer-for-a-day/

item.title: “Tren de Sóller” added in Palma, Spain
item.description: Historic electric train over the mountains, with street running in Palma. Plus opening windows and balcony flailing opportunities. Connects to vintage trams in Sóller. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xf01u3u8I4c

item.title: “Zagreb TV Tower” added in Gornja Bistra, Croatia
item.description: Get the cable car up to the TV tower and then go up the TV tower.

item.description: Shop that sells train related items

item.title: “GENERAL STORE RAILYARD 秋葉原” added in Akihabara, Japan

“Paris Sewer Museum” added in Levallois-Perret, France
item.description: A vast museum in the sewers, with old equipment to see. Signs are in French, but they can give you a book with English translations to borrow.

item.description:
University built around a former steelworks (with museum)

item.description: Big saltworks where you can get a tour either on a bike or an a little train

“Transparent Public Toilets - Tokyo Toilet #7” added in Motoyoyogichō, Japan
“Sasazuka Greenway Public Toilets - The Tokyo Toilet #1” added in Sasazuka, Japan
“JAL Sky Museum” added in Haneda, Japan
item.description: Small museum with historical uniforms/memorabilia/gift shop followed by a tour of the JAL maintenance hangars where you get to see people at work maintaining JAL's fleet. Reservations need to be made a month in advance, and whilst the museum exhibits are bi-lingual it may be worth emailing after making a reservation to specify that you'd prefer an English-speaking guide if one's available (unless your Japanese is good enough to understand the safety instructions and plane facts!)

item.title: “Osaka Monorail Banpaku-Kinen-Koen Station” added in Ibaraki, Japan
item.description: This station is served by both the Osaka Monorail main line as well as the Saito branch line - which means to the east there's a remarkable set of switchable monorail track which can be fun to watch as trains come in and out of the station as sections of the track rearrange themselves. Trains from the branch line normally terminate here, but run through to Senri-Chuo station during the peaks.

item.title: “Natural History Museum Rotterdam” added in Rotterdam, Netherlands
item.description: Contains a permanent collection of 'famous' dead animals, including a stone marten that once snuck into and shut down the Large Hadron Collider at CERN, and a swallow that was shot after knocking over 23,000 dominoes.

item.title: “Omoide Yokocho Memory Lane” added in Kabukicho, Japan
item.description: Another street of tiny bars, also known as piss alley.

item.title: “Fuji Television Headquarters “HACHITAMA” Spherical Observation Room” added in Daiba, Japan
item.description: Building with a big "ball" in it, has a observation deck.

item.title: “Gate Tower Building” added in Umeda, Japan
item.description: Building with a highway running through it

item.title: “Stourbridge Junction - Unique train shuttle to Stourbridge Town” added in Stourbridge, United Kingdom
item.description: Class 139 - it's like a minibus on wheels and flywheel powered! Fun 3 min trip. Plus you might catch George the station cat while you're there.

item.title: “Diglis Fish Pass” added in Worcester, United Kingdom
item.description: Only open on select days, sometimes needing booking far in advance. Check before you travel.

item.title: “Tank Traps” added in Ashford, United Kingdom
item.description: A bunch of tank arranged behind a hedge on the edge of a park.

item.title: “Owyhee County Museum & Library” added in Murphy, United States
item.description:
Delightful museum with a complex of buildings. Includes an entire room with thousands (?) of wrenches from a local's collection, and another local's collection of wagons. Plus an unrestored caboose you can enter, and a print shop with linotype presses.
added by jt

item.title: “Hindenburgdamm” added in Morsum, Germany
item.description: 11 km long rail-only causeway linking seaside holiday island of Sylt to the German mainland. Carries passenger trains and double deck car shuttles.

item.title: “CERN Animal Shelter for Computer Mice” added in Satigny, Switzerland
item.description:
You may be able to see this while on a site tour at CERN. (Some tours go past this, but some don't.)
https://computer-animal-shelter.web.cern.ch/index.shtml

item.title: “CERN” added in Meyrin, Switzerland
item.description: Site tours are available, which are interesting. There's also an exhibition space, which includes the original NeXT computer used by Sir Tim Berners-Lee to design the World Wide Web and host the first web page at CERN on 25 December 1990.

item.title: “AKW Zwentendorf” added in Zwentendorf, Austria
item.description: Nuclear power plant that was built but never used. Tours are possible but book out fast

item.title: “Innsbruck Airport history room” added in Völs, Austria
item.description: Just a small room exhibiting information about the airport's history

item.title: “Nordbahntrasse” added in Wuppertal, Germany
